newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-DRUMMOND A MAN APART ON THE ATHLETICS CIRCUIT.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-DRUMMOND A MAN APART ON THE ATHLETICS CIRCUIT.

text.p: Jon Drummond talks almost as good a race as his training partner Ato Boldon.
But his reasons for running a great race differ from Boldon's and just about everyone else's at the sixth world championships starting on Saturday.
The 28-year-old American, the self-proclaimed "Clown Prince of the Track", was born with spina bifida and there were real fears he would not be able to walk, let alone run, in later life.

But gradually the condition improved, and since the age of two, he has never stopped running. Now, as one of the world's top sprinters, he owns an Olympic relay silver medal and world championship relay gold.
Drummond, the American 200 champion, has a realistic chance of claiming his first individual world championship title here.
Like Boldon, he is coached by John Smith and believes Smith has helped him take him to the verge of inheriting the title from fellow-American Michael Johnson.
But he laughed off a suggestion on Friday that the 200 was a weak event because the defending champion had opted for the 400 instead.
"Michael Johnson might not be running, but Frankie Fredericks is and Frankie beat Michael in every race after the Olympics last year and Frankie is going to be in the race," Drummond said.
"So to say the 200 is weak is to say that Frankie Fredericks is weak -- and you had better ask Frankie what he thinks about that."
Drummond's father was a clergyman, he has studied karate and also sang lead tenor in a band called Kirk Franklin and the Family who had a number one hit in the Billboard Gospel chart in 1993.

His philosophy on the track is encapsulated in a trademark smile which he flashes whether he wins or loses. In many respects, he really has an Olympian spirit, taking part because he loves to compete.
"I really do love track and field. I'm a fan of the sport as well as a competitor and I think my desire for running is different from everyone else's.
"The fact that I am running is a blessing from God and so when you see me smile it's because I am happy I can run. I'm happy I am walking I am happy that I am just alive.

"Some people are here because they want the medals, I want those things too but the fact that I am say, one out of 30 million, who have made the team from how I started off in life has got to make me happy.
"This is my opportunity to show to the American public and to the world who I am and what I represent."
Drummond may differ from many athletes in many respects, but he is not averse to trying to hype himself and psyche out his opponents.
After describing just what a force Fredericks will be to beat, he promptly dismissed him from the final reckoning.
Asked how he saw the battle for the 200 developing he said: "I don't intend to watch much of it because in most of my races I intend to be running out in the front.
"I think me, Boldon and my colleague Gentry Bradley will go 1-2-3. It'll be a sweep."
